rules.title: Housing Application Criminal Record Inquiries Prohibited Prior to Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application containing inquiries regarding criminal records prior to providing a conditional offer. A housing provider may only inquire about convictions for methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.exemptions:
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.; Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Pre-Offer Criminal Record Inquiries Prohibited
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

rules.title: Applicant Submission of Inaccuracy or Rehabilitation Evidence
rules.requirement: An applicant may submit evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies in the criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation and other mitigating factors.
rules.quoted_span:
An applicant
may provide evidence to the housing
provider demonstrating inaccuracies within the applicant's criminal record or
evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.title: Written Disclosures Required Prior to Accepting Application Fee
rules.requirement: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review and consideration of criminal history, and that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
Prior to
accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to
the applicant:
(1)   Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing
provider include the review and consideration of criminal history; and
(2)   A statement that the applicant, pursuant to
subsection a. of this section, may provide evidence demonstrating inaccuracies
within the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.

rules.title: Nondiscriminatory Application of Application Standards
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall apply the statutory application process standards to each applicant in a nondiscriminatory manner.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider
shall apply the standards established by this section to each applicant in a
nondiscriminatory manner.

rules.title: Prohibited Criminal Records in Applicant Evaluation
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not evaluate an applicant, either before or after a conditional offer, based on arrests or charges not resulting in conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile delinquency adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]

rules.title: Permissible Criminal Records After Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: After issuing a conditional offer, a housing provider may only consider convictions for specified major offenses or lifetime sex offender registration, or indictable offenses within defined time limits: first degree within six years, second or third degree within four years, and fourth degree within one year.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
After the issuance of a conditional offer to an
applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the
applicant’s history that:
(1)   resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated
sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in
violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a
prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of
paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in
lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry;
(2)   is for an indictable offense of the first degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of
the conditional offer;
(3)   is for an indictable offense of the second or
third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison
sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding
the issuance of the conditional offer; or
(4)   is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the
conditional offer.

rules.title: Standard for Withdrawing Conditional Offer Based on Criminal Record
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if it determines by a preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a
conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing
provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is
necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.

rules.title: Written Notice and Opportunity to Appeal Withdrawal
rules.requirement: Upon withdrawing a conditional offer, a housing provider must provide the applicant with written notice stating specific reasons for the withdrawal and offering an opportunity to appeal by submitting evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
If a housing provider withdraws a conditional
offer, the housing provider shall provide the applicant with written
notification that includes, with specificity, the reason or reasons for the
withdrawal of the conditional offer and an opportunity to appeal the denial by
providing evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies within
the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.

rules.title: Individualized Assessment Factors Before Withdrawal
rules.requirement: The housing provider must perform an individualized assessment considering the offense's nature and severity, applicant's age at occurrence, time elapsed, rehabilitation evidence, safety risks if reoccurring, and whether the offense occurred on or was connected to rented property.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
The housing provider shall perform an
individualized assessment of the application in light of the following factors:
(a)   the nature and severity of the criminal offense;
(b)   the age of the applicant at the time of the
occurrence of the criminal offense;
(c)   the time which has elapsed since the occurrence
of the criminal offense;
(d)   any information produced by the applicant, or
produced on the applicant's behalf, in regard to the applicant's rehabilitation
and good conduct since the occurrence of the criminal offense;
(e)   the degree to which the criminal offense, if it
reoccurred, would negatively impact the safety of the housing provider's other
tenants or property; and
(f)   whether the criminal offense occurred on or was
connected to property that was rented or leased by the applicant.

rules.title: Applicant Request and Duty to Provide Relied-Upon Information
rules.requirement: An applicant may request within 30 days of withdrawal notice a copy of all information relied upon by the housing provider, which the housing provider must provide free of charge within 10 days of receiving the request.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
The applicant may request, within 30 days
after the housing provider's notice of the withdrawal, that the housing
provider afford the applicant a copy of all information that the housing
provider relied upon in considering the applicant, including criminal records.
(2)   A housing provider shall provide the information
requested under paragraph (1) of this subsection, free of charge, within l0
days after receipt of a timely request.

rules.title: Discriminatory Advertisements Regarding Criminal History Prohibited
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish any advertisement explicitly stating that applicants with arrests or convictions will not be considered, except regarding methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.

except

registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.; Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except
for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Unlawful Discriminatory Statements, Signs, Applications, or Inquiries Prohibited
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not print, publish, display, or circulate any statement, ad, sign, application form, or make any inquiry expressing any unlawful limitation or discrimination based on criminal record, except as permitted by the act and for methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing or lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.exemptions:
except as permitted by this act and
for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of
methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the
applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex
offender registration program.; Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider
shall not print, publish, circulate, issue, display, post, or mail, or cause to
be printed, published, circulated, issued, displayed, posted or mailed any
statement, advertisement, publication or sign, or use any form of application
for the rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion
thereof or make any record or inquiry in connection with the prospective
rental, lease, or sublease of any real property or part or portion thereof
which expresses, directly or indirectly, any unlawful limitation, specification
or discrimination as to criminal record, except as permitted by this act and
for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of
methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the
applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex
offender registration program.

rules.title: Confidentiality and Permissible Use of Applicant Criminal Records
rules.requirement: Unless required by law, a housing provider shall not distribute an applicant's criminal record to anyone not expected to use it consistently with this act, nor use it for any inconsistent purpose.
rules.exemptions:
Unless otherwise
required by law; Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
Unless otherwise
required by law, a housing provider shall not:
(1)   distribute or
disseminate an applicant’s criminal record to any person who is not expected to
use the criminal record for the purpose of evaluating the applicant in a manner
consistent with this act; or
(2)   use an applicant’s
criminal record for a purpose that is not consistent with this act
.

rules.title: Prohibition on Drug or Alcohol Testing and Treatment Facility Inquiries
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant's consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Interference and Retaliation Prohibited
rules.requirement: No person shall interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of any right protected under this act, and any retaliatory action taken against a person for filing a complaint shall be enforced as a separate violation.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A person shall not interfere with, restrain, or
deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right protected under
this act.  If the division determines that a housing provider has engaged in
one or more unlawful actions against a person with the intent of retaliating
for the person’s filing of an action against the housing provider pursuant to
section 12 of this act, then each unlawful retaliatory action shall be
enforced, pursuant to section 12 of this act, as a separate and distinct
violation of this act.

rules.title: Eviction Grounds and Notice Following Overturned Remedial Housing Order
rules.requirement: If a court overturns a director's order that provided housing to an applicant, that determination constitutes grounds for the housing provider to evict the former applicant, provided the housing provider gives at least 45 days' notice prior to eviction.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.interaction: Overrides the Anti-Eviction Act, P.L.1974, c.49 (C.2A:18-61.1 et seq.), making a successful appeal that overturns a final decision of the director grounds for eviction with at least 45 days' notice.
rules.quoted_span:
Notwithstanding any provision of the Anti-Eviction Act, P.L.1974, c.49
(C.2A:18-61.1 et seq.) to the contrary, if an appeal by a
housing provider is successful, and the court overturns a final decision of the
director that resulted in an order under this paragraph, then a determination
that the housing provider did not violate the provisions of this act as evidenced
by such successful appeal shall be grounds for the housing provider to evict
the former applicant if that person resides in a rental dwelling unit owned by
the housing provider as the result of the director’s order, so long as the
housing provider provides the applicant with at least 45 days’ notice prior to
the eviction;

rules.title: Remedy of Conditional Offer or Rental Unit for Repeat Violations
rules.requirement: If a housing provider committed at least one other violation of the act within the preceding five years, the director may order it to make a good faith effort to remedy the violation by issuing a conditional offer or providing the same or a similar rental dwelling unit on the same terms as the prior conditional offer.
rules.coverage_conditions: housing provider has committed at least one other violation of this act within the preceding five-year period
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
If a housing provider has committed at least one
other violation of this act within the preceding five-year period, the director
may require the housing provider to make a good faith effort to remedy the
violation with respect to the applicant when a remedy is possible, by issuing a
conditional offer, if the violation has resulted in a failure to issue a
conditional offer, or by providing the same or a similar rental dwelling unit
to the applicant on the same terms as the prior conditional offer if the same
or a similar rental dwelling unit is currently or will become available, if the
violation has resulted in the withdrawal of a conditional offer.

rules.title: Application Fee Return and Monetary Relief Remedies
rules.requirement: Unless housing is provided to the applicant as a remedy, the director may require the housing provider to return the applicant's application fee, and may require up to $1,000 of the penalty owed by the housing provider to be paid to the applicant.
rules.exemptions: Unless housing is provided to the applicant pursuant to paragraph (2) of this subsection; Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
Unless housing is provided to the applicant
pursuant to paragraph (2) of this subsection, the director may require that the
applicant’s rental application fee be returned; and
(4)   The director may require that a portion of the
sum owed by the housing provider pursuant to subsection c. of this section be
paid to the applicant in an amount not to exceed $1,000.
